My reports

Every report is an application to the authorities. It stays “In review” until the Vigilância Ambiental has checked the site. Only then does it count as a confirmed breeding site, so nobody can claim something without it being verified. Tap an application to delete it.

Which vaccine, and for whom?

As of October 2026

Qdenga (Takeda), 2 doses 3 months apart. Free in the SUS for children and teenagers aged 10 to 14. The vaccine is licensed for ages 4 to 60, including people who have had dengue before.

Butantan-DV, the world's first single-dose dengue vaccine, was introduced in January 2026 for people aged 15 to 59. On 8 June 2026 the Ministry of Health paused it as a precaution to investigate cases with severe symptoms after vaccination. A causal link had not been confirmed at that point. People who are already vaccinated are still considered protected.

Priority: older and high-risk people first

Older people and people at higher risk are given priority for dengue vaccination.

  • Butantan-DV: the Ministry of Health started with the oldest eligible age (59 years) and then moved down step by step towards 15 years.
  • Health workers in primary care were among the first groups vaccinated.
  • Qdenga in the SUS goes to ages 10 to 14, an age group with many hospital admissions.
  • If you are older or have a chronic illness, ask at your UBS or a CRIE whether and when you can get vaccinated.

Sources: IstoÉ Dinheiro: Ministry of Health vaccination strategy · Afya: Butantan-DV rollout from age 59 · Afya: health workers vaccinated first · BandNews: Qdenga for ages 10–14

Sources: TNH1: Who can get the dengue vaccine (Jan 2026) · SBIm: Qdenga questions and answers · BandNews: Butantan-DV rollout (Jan 2026) · Instituto Butantan: pause of Butantan-DV

Risks: the disease vs. the vaccine

The disease: Most infections are mild, but severe dengue can kill. In Brazil, about 4.4% of severe cases in 2024 were fatal (as of April 2024). In Rio Grande do Sul, 73% of the first 73 deaths in 2024 were people aged 60 or older. Deaths occurred on average 8.3 days after the first symptoms, so early treatment matters.

The vaccine (Qdenga): very common side effects are pain and redness at the injection site, headache, muscle pain, feeling unwell, weakness and fever. Not for pregnant or breastfeeding women or people with a weakened immune system, because it is a live attenuated vaccine. Efficacy in the clinical trials: about 80%.

Sources: WHO: Dengue and severe dengue · Olhar Digital: dengue deaths 2024 · Governo do RS: profile of 2024 dengue deaths · Qdenga patient leaflet (Takeda) · SBIm: Qdenga questions and answers · Jornal de Brasília: Qdenga prices and efficacy

Do I have dengue?

Tap a number on the body to see the symptom, then mark the ones you have. Typical: high fever (39–40 °C) for 2 to 7 days with at least two other symptoms.

Warning signs (usually between day 3 and 7, when the fever drops)
Have you been in an area with dengue in the last 14 days?
Are you in a risk group?

This check does not replace a medical examination. If you suspect dengue, do not take aspirin or ibuprofen, which increase the risk of bleeding.

Sources: WHO: Dengue and severe dengue · Ministério da Saúde: Dengue FAQ · SES-RS via Sul21: dengue symptoms · CNN Brasil / SBI: medicines to avoid

Alerts

Alerts

Flood forecast

Mosquito risk rises about 7 to 14 days after the water goes down. That is how long Aedes aegypti needs from egg to biting mosquito. Forecasts here are simulated.

Official warnings: text your postcode (CEP) to 40199 to get free Defesa Civil SMS alerts.

Sources: Fiocruz/IOC: Dengue leaflet · Governo do RS: Defesa Civil SMS alerts

Important notice

Not a medical diagnosis

Rede Viva provides general information only. The symptom check and all health content in this app are guidance, not a diagnosis.

  • If you have symptoms or any health concern, always get the opinion of a doctor or specialist.
  • Do not start, stop or change any treatment based on this app.
  • In an emergency, call SAMU on 192 or go to the nearest UPA or hospital.
